§5.3 Input + output (funciones como puente entre entrada léxica y producción oral)
§5.4 Fluency vs accuracy — S5 privilegia fluency (post-task delayed feedback)
§5.6 Drilling & backchaining — frases fijas funcionales memorizadas
§5.8 Feedback diferenciado — fluency dominante + recast sutil en breakdowns
§5.9 Gestión del L1 — 12% (caídas sólo para meta-instrucción carousel + causal 'because')
§5.10 SUCCESS vocabulary — 10 chunks funcionales cerrando la apropiación
§5.13 Noticing del stress — 6 palabras stress marking (beCAUSE, exCUSE me, THANK you...)
§9.2 Grammar carga — Gr 15 (conectores) Intro + Gr 1-5, 14 Consolida
descriptores_cefr_activos: A1.1 — Can introduce self and others with formulaic greetings
A1.1 — Can identify and name studio objects using 'this is / that is'
A1.1 — Can describe objects with basic adjectives (be + adjective)
A1.1 — Can give and follow simple imperative instructions
A1.1 — Can request clarification with fixed formulas (repeat please, again)
A1.1 — Can express basic preferences (I like + noun)
A1.1 — Can link 2 short sentences with and/but/or/because

universe_anchor.narrative_universe: Pixel & Ink Studio — boutique design studio in Bogotá
characters_active_in_s5: Sophia Vargas — Art Director (welcomes the junior designers, gives briefs)
Andrés Ruiz — Junior Designer (learner avatar, introduces self, asks for clarification)
Diego López — Print Producer (gives instructions about files and paper)
Client — Don Pedro (La Esquina Bakery) enters briefly for scenario E
scenarios_in_s5: SCN-A: First day at the studio — introductions round
SCN-B: Morning briefing — Sophia names the materials of the day
SCN-C: Pair work — Andrés and Laura describe fonts and colors
SCN-D: Print workshop — Diego gives save/export instructions
SCN-E: Quick client intake — Don Pedro drops off reference and asks questions

integration_all_archetypes_policy.directive: Quiero todos los arquetipos para todos los PM — compendio metodológico del instructor.
integration_all_archetypes_policy.rationale_a11: Los 5 arquetipos existen como OPCIONES del instructor. A1.1 requiere andamiaje alto, por lo que cada arquetipo se presenta con frases fijas + Language Bank + Micro-Cápsulas, en lugar de producción libre. El instructor elige un FLOW de rotación (ver abajo) para determinar cuál(es) arquetipo(s) ejecuta en la sesión real.
integration_all_archetypes_policy.bloom_ceiling_a11: L3 Apply máximo — ningún arquetipo exige analizar/evaluar/crear sin soporte.

the_function_toolkit.description_bilingual: Five function families from PM-1.2, packaged into 5 quiz sections. El aprendiz domina estas cinco familias y puede trabajar en el studio. *El aprendiz domina estas cinco familias y puede trabajar en el estudio.*

function_families.name: SOCIALIZING — Greetings & Self-Introduction
function_families.source_pm12: Greetings and introductions + Giving personal information
exponents_fixed_phrases: I am [Name]. I am a junior designer.
My program is [program]. My shift is [morning/afternoon].
function_families.studio_micro_example: SOPHIA: Good morning. Welcome to Pixel & Ink. | ANDRÉS: Hello, I am Andrés. I am a junior designer. Nice to meet you.

function_families.name: IDENTIFICATION — Naming Objects
function_families.source_pm12: Naming and identifying objects in the design studio (This is a…, That is a…)
exponents_fixed_phrases: Is this a [object]? — Yes, it is. / No, it is not.
What is this? — It is a [object].
function_families.studio_micro_example: LAURA: Look. This is a tablet. That is a stylus. These are sketchbooks.

function_families.name: DESCRIPTION — Basic Adjectives
function_families.source_pm12: Describing everyday design objects with basic adjectives
exponents_fixed_phrases: It is big / small / thin / thick.
The logo is round and blue.
function_families.studio_micro_example: ANDRÉS: The logo is round. The color is warm. The font is serif and big.

function_families.name: INSTRUCTIONS — Imperatives
function_families.source_pm12: Following and giving simple workshop instructions
function_families.studio_micro_example: DIEGO: Open the file. Save the document. Close the app. Please click on Export.

function_families.name: REPAIR & PREFERENCE — Clarification + Likes
exponents_fixed_phrases: I like [noun]. / I like blue. / I like serif fonts.
function_families.grammar_target: Gr 5 (imperative: repeat) + Gr 1 (I am / I like)
function_families.studio_micro_example: ANDRÉS: Sorry, I do not understand. Repeat, please. | SOPHIA: I said: save the file. | ANDRÉS: OK. I like blue and I like serif fonts.

connector_bridge_gr15.intro_context: Gr 15 (PM-0 §9.2 Intro for S5): connectors and / but / or / because + basic punctuation. Se introducen para enlazar los 5 exponentes funcionales en oraciones compuestas simples A1.1.

connectors_active.example: I am Andrés AND I am a designer.
The font is big BUT the color is soft.
Save the file OR close the app.
I like Helvetica BECAUSE it is clean.

archetype_a_information_exchange.name: ARCHETYPE A — Information Exchange

pre_function.bilingual_unified: Look at your Studio Card. *Mira tu Tarjeta de Estudio.*
pre_function.setup: Cada aprendiz recibe una tarjeta con 8 objetos del studio (tablet, stylus, font, logo, etc.). Las tarjetas del Aprendiz A y Aprendiz B tienen 5 diferencias (color, tamaño, forma).
pre_function.review_exponents: Revisa las frases fijas de FUNC-2 y FUNC-3 (2 minutos).

sequence: 1. Sit back-to-back with your partner (*Siéntate espalda con espalda con tu compañero*).
2. Student A describes: 'In my card, the logo is BIG and ROUND.' Student B compares: 'In my card, the logo is SMALL and SQUARE. Different!'
3. Find 5 differences in 8 minutes. Use only English. Use the chunks: 'In my card...', 'The X is Y', 'Different / Same'.
4. Pair reports to class: 'We found 5 differences. The logo is big in A but small in B.'
Complete the 4-cell organizer: CAUSE → EFFECT using 'because'.
Example rows pre-filled:
• Effect: 'I like Helvetica' ← Cause: 'it is clean' → Sentence: 'I like Helvetica BECAUSE it is clean.'
• Effect: 'The color is warm' ← Cause: 'it is red and orange' → Sentence: 'The color is warm BECAUSE it is red and orange.'
Students generate 2 more rows using studio objects.
Verbalize aloud with stress on beCAUSE.
Expert Groups (4 students per group, 4 topics): TYPOGRAPHY / COLOR / TOOLS / COMPOSITION.
Each expert group masters 4 identification sentences about their topic (3 min).
Home Groups re-form (1 expert per topic).
Each expert teaches the other 3 using 'This is a...', 'It is...', 'Because...' (A1.1 fixed chunks). Time: 2 min per expert.

post_function_reflection.question_bilingual: Which chunk did you use the most? *¿Qué frase usaste más?*
post_function_reflection.self_rating_0_2: 0 = I did not use it | 1 = I used it with errors | 2 = I used it correctly.

archetype_a_information_exchange.micro_capsule: > 💬 **Function Rule:** 'because' answers WHY. It is stressed on the 2nd syllable: be-CAUSE.
archetype_a_information_exchange.plan_b: Si solo 1 parte funciona: mantén Spot the Difference (es la más resistente a niveles mixtos A1.1).

archetype_b_persuasion_argumentation.name: ARCHETYPE B — Persuasion & Argumentation (A1.1 scaffolded)
techniques_active: Third Conditional Debate — NOT APPLICABLE at A1.1
functions_activated: FUNC-5 Preference (I like / I do not like)
archetype_b_persuasion_argumentation.a11_adaptation_warning: A1.1 no puede persuadir con registro retórico. Se adapta a 'STUDIO PREFERENCE DEFENSE' — defender una elección de diseño con 2 razones causales.

pre_function.bilingual_unified: Choose one studio object. *Elige un objeto del estudio.*
pre_function.setup: Cada aprendiz elige 1 de 5 objetos (Helvetica font / Times New Roman font / Red color / Blue color / Round logo). Deberá defender por qué es la mejor elección para una cafetería (La Esquina Bakery).

function_practice_preference_defense.technique: Studio Preference Defense (Speech Writers adaptado A1.1)
sequence: 1. Fill the defense card: 'I recommend [object] for La Esquina Bakery. I like [object] because [reason 1] and [reason 2].'
2. Example model: 'I recommend Helvetica for La Esquina Bakery. I like Helvetica because it is clean AND it is modern.'
3. Each student delivers 30 seconds of defense to a partner.
4. Partner reacts with one of: 'I agree. It is [adjective].' / 'I do not agree. I like [alternative] more.'
function_practice_preference_defense.defense_sentence_frame: I recommend ____. I like ____ because ____ and ____.

sequence: Optional — if technology available.
AI prompt: 'You are a client. Ask the student: What color is best for a bakery logo? React with 2 short questions in A1 English.'
Student defends with: 'I like [color] because [reason].' and answers 2 follow-ups.
Duration: 2 min per student.
a11_ai_rules: AI must use CEFR A1 output

archetype_b_persuasion_argumentation.micro_capsule: > 💬 **Defense Rule:** At A1.1, persuasion = 1 preference + 1 because + 1 and. That is enough.
archetype_b_persuasion_argumentation.plan_b: Si Arquetipo B se siente demasiado abstracto, colapsar a una sola 'like/don't like + because' ronda.

archetype_c_social_interpersonal.name: ARCHETYPE C — Social & Interpersonal

pre_function.bilingual_unified: Stand up. Form a circle. *De pie. Formen un círculo.*
pre_function.setup: Toda la clase de pie en círculo. Sophia (rol del instructor) abre el 'First day at the studio'.

sequence: 1. Round 1 (2 min): Each student in order says: 'Good morning. I am [name]. I am a junior designer. Nice to meet you.'
2. Round 2 (3 min): Extend with one preference: '... and I like [color/font/tool].'

3. Round 3 (4 min): Chain memory — each student repeats the previous 2 students' preferences before adding their own. 'She is María and she likes blue. He is Juan and he likes Helvetica. I am Andrés and I like serif fonts.'
4. Line-up variant: re-order the class by 'month of birth' using 'My birthday is in [month]'.
function_practice_introduction_chain.backchaining_drill: Backchain 'Nice to meet you': 'you → meet you → to meet you → Nice to meet you.'

sequence: 1. Pairs. Student A is JUNIOR DESIGNER. Student B is ART DIRECTOR.
2. Junior complaint cards (choose 1): 'The file is big.' / 'The font is small.' / 'The color is cold.' / 'The computer is slow.'
3. Art Director response card (fixed): 'Sorry. I can help. Open the menu and click on [option].'
4. Complete 4 rounds with role swap. Use 'but' to soften: 'The file is big, but I can try.'
function_practice_endless_complaints.fixed_phrases_ban_paraphrase: Los aprendices deben usar las frases fijas — no pueden reformular libremente (A1.1).

function_practice_paraphrasing_relay.technique: Paraphrasing Relay — Explain Like I'm 10 (A1.1 version)
sequence: 1. Target word hidden: 'tablet'.
2. Student A describes using FUNC-3 chunks WITHOUT saying 'tablet': 'It is black. It is thin. It is small. I draw on it.'
3. Student B guesses. If no guess, Student A adds: 'The screen is glass.'
4. Words to paraphrase: tablet / stylus / folder / menu / logo.

post_function_reflection.question_bilingual: Which function was easiest? Which was hardest? *¿Qué función fue más fácil? ¿Cuál más difícil?*
post_function_reflection.target: Acknowledge repair chunks ('Repeat please') as survival tools, not weakness.

archetype_c_social_interpersonal.micro_capsule: > 💬 **Social Rule:** Saying 'Repeat please' is NOT weakness. It is the number-one survival skill of A1.1 designers.
archetype_c_social_interpersonal.plan_b: Si la energía baja, saltar directamente a Introduction Chain Round 3 (Chain Memory) — es el más lúdico.

archetype_d_gamified.name: ARCHETYPE D — Gamified Functions
techniques_active: Survival Game — NOT APPLICABLE at A1.1

pre_function.bilingual_unified: You are trapped in the studio. The door closes in 10 minutes. *Están atrapados en el estudio. La puerta se cierra en 10 minutos.*
pre_function.setup: Narrativa de escape: 'Sophia left a puzzle. Solve 5 clues to get the key (a USB with the final logo).'

function_practice_escape_room.technique: Studio Escape Room — 5 clues map to FUNC-1→FUNC-5

clues.task: Find the designer named 'Laura'. Introduce yourself correctly. She gives you clue 2.
clues.pass_criterion: 'Good morning. I am [name]. Nice to meet you.' — 3 chunks correct.

clues.task: On the wall, 6 tools are unlabeled. Name them correctly in 60 seconds.
clues.fail_consequence: Laura gives a hint in English: 'Not brush. Think thin.'

clues.task: Decode Sophia's note: 'The key is BIG, BLUE, and ROUND.' Find the matching object among 10.
clues.pass_criterion: Correct object found using 2 descriptors (A1.1 simplified).

clues.task: Follow Diego's audio instructions: 'Open the drawer. Take the red folder. Open the folder. Find the USB.'
Ask Sophia (instructor) 3 questions to finish: 'What is this? Repeat please. I like [X] or [Y]?'
clues.fail_consequence: No penalty — this is the reward stage.

function_practice_escape_room.win_condition: All 5 clues solved → team receives printable 'Pixel & Ink Survivor Certificate'.

sequence: AI prompt: 'You are Don Pedro, client of La Esquina Bakery. Speak only in A1 English. Ask the designer: What is your name? What color do you like? Can you help me?'
Student roleplays as junior designer Andrés. Uses: Introduction + Description + Preference + 'I can help.'
Duration: 3 min per student. Max 5 exchanges.

post_function_debrief.question_bilingual_1: What function did you use without thinking? *¿Qué función usaste sin pensar?*
post_function_debrief.question_bilingual_2: Did the clock help or block you? *¿El reloj te ayudó o te bloqueó?*
post_function_debrief.takeaway: Under pressure, fixed phrases emerged automatically. This is fluency in birth.

archetype_d_gamified.micro_capsule: > 🎮 **Game Rule:** The escape room forces the chunks to come out. If you do not say 'Repeat please' you lose the clue. Survival = speaking.
archetype_d_gamified.plan_b: Si no hay tiempo/recursos para escape room completo, ejecutar solo Clue 2 + Clue 4 (20 min total).

archetype_e_academic_discourse.name: ARCHETYPE E — Academic & Discourse (A1.1 proto-academic)
techniques_active: Socratic Seminar — NOT APPLICABLE at A1.1
archetype_e_academic_discourse.a11_adaptation_warning: A1.1 no puede hacer discurso académico real. Se adapta a 'MICRO-SYNTHESIS' — sintetizar 3 fuentes (3 tarjetas) en un resumen oral de 30 segundos.

pre_function.bilingual_unified: Read 3 cards about Helvetica. *Lee 3 tarjetas sobre Helvetica.*
pre_function.setup: Cada equipo recibe 3 tarjetas A1.1 sobre un objeto (ej: Helvetica / Red color / Round logo). Cada tarjeta tiene 2 frases.
example_cards_helvetica: Card 1: Helvetica is a sans-serif font. It is clean.
Card 2: Designers use Helvetica on posters. It is modern.
Card 3: Helvetica is on signs in the airport. It is big.

sequence: 1. Team reads 3 cards (2 min).
2. Team fuses cards into a 30-second speech using: 'Helvetica is a sans-serif font and it is clean. Designers use it on posters and signs. It is clean AND modern BECAUSE it is simple.'
3. One team member delivers the speech. Class listens.
4. Connectors required: and (2x) + because (1x).
function_practice_micro_synthesis.synthesis_frame: [Object] is [type]. Designers use it [where]. It is [adj1] AND [adj2] BECAUSE it is [reason].

function_practice_mini_jigsaw.technique: Mini Expert Jigsaw (same as Archetype A but with academic framing)
sequence: Expert Groups master 1 of 4 topics: FONT FAMILIES / COLOR TEMPERATURE / LOGO SHAPES / COMPOSITION.
Home Groups re-form. Each expert teaches using: 'This is [topic]. It has [element 1] AND [element 2]. It is important BECAUSE [reason].'
Peer rating (0-2): understandable / connectors used / fluent.

post_function_metadiscourse.prompt: Complete: 'I synthesized 3 cards about ____. The main idea is: it is ____ AND ____ BECAUSE ____.'
post_function_metadiscourse.meta_awareness: Students notice they DID academic discourse — just in 30 seconds at A1.1.

archetype_e_academic_discourse.micro_capsule: > 📚 **Academic Rule:** At A1.1, academic = 3 facts + 2 connectors + 1 because. That is a synthesis.
archetype_e_academic_discourse.plan_b: Si Arquetipo E se siente pesado, hacer solo micro-synthesis (el jigsaw ya se hizo en Arquetipo A).

rotation_flows_for_instructor.directive_reminder: El instructor ELIGE uno o combina. No se ejecutan los 5 en la misma sesión.

flow_f1_social_game.name: FLOW-F1 — Social + Game (RECOMMENDED A1.1)
flow_f1_social_game.target: Máxima energía + memoria afectiva para fijar FUNC-1/2/4/5
flow_f1_social_game.when_to_choose: Grupos principiantes, primera guía del programa, grupos tímidos

flow_f2_information_defense.name: FLOW-F2 — Information + Defense
flow_f2_information_defense.when_to_choose: Grupos con perfil más analítico / programas con componente teórico

flow_f3_academic_prep.name: FLOW-F3 — Academic Prep
flow_f3_academic_prep.target: Preparar para programas tecnológicos con componente EAP
flow_f3_academic_prep.when_to_choose: Grupos que siguen a un nivel A2+ con escritura académica

flow_f4_evidence_laser.name: FLOW-F4 — Evidence Laser (para E5 directa)
flow_f4_evidence_laser.sequence: Archetype C (Introduction Chain Round 3) → Role Carousel (5 estaciones) + rúbrica E5
flow_f4_evidence_laser.target: Maximizar probabilidad de E5 aprobada en 1 sesión
flow_f4_evidence_laser.when_to_choose: Si la S5 es la única ventana para generar E5 con rúbrica

flow_f5_maximalist.name: FLOW-F5 — Maximalist (los 5 arquetipos en mini-dosis)
flow_f5_maximalist.target: Paseo metodológico por las 5 familias de funciones
flow_f5_maximalist.when_to_choose: Grupos maduros con alta energía, última sesión antes de consolidación

role_carousel_design_for_e5_evidence.description: Role Carousel = instrumento canónico para E5. 5 estaciones × 90 segundos × rotación.

stations.name: SOCIALIZE (FUNC-1)
stations.scenario: First day welcome. Greet Sophia and 2 team members.

stations.name: IDENTIFY (FUNC-2)
stations.scenario: Name 5 studio objects on the desk.

stations.name: DESCRIBE (FUNC-3)
stations.scenario: Describe the La Esquina Bakery logo to a pair.

stations.name: INSTRUCT (FUNC-4)
stations.scenario: Give 4 imperatives to save and export a file.

role_carousel_design_for_e5_evidence.rubric_instrument_reference: Escala de estimación No 5 — Language Functions (derivada por PM-4.1)

success_factors_application.Salience: Capitalized stress markers on teacher board + physical gestures (hand up for 'Repeat please')
success_factors_application.Use: Every station forces at least 2 uses per chunk
success_factors_application.Connection: Each chunk linked to a scenario character (Sophia = welcomes, Don Pedro = excuses, Diego = finished)
success_factors_application.Emotion: Escape Room pressure + laughter in Introduction Chain Round 3
success_factors_application.Spaced_repetition: Chunks from S1-S4 re-cycled in every archetype
success_factors_application.Synergy: Chunks of FUNC-1 combine with FUNC-5 (greet → ask to repeat → thank you)

activities.statement: Ejecutar 5 funciones comunicativas del designer junior (Socializing, Identification, Description, Instructions, Repair + Preference) en escenarios del Pixel & Ink Studio usando frases fijas + conectores and/but/or/because.
activities.didactic_strategy: Juego de roles + Simulación rotativa (Role Carousel)
activities.didactic_technique: Dramatización + Think-Pair-Share + Introduction Chain + Spot the Difference

activities.statement: Reflexionar sobre el uso autónomo de funciones comunicativas identificando qué chunks se producen automáticamente bajo presión y cuáles requieren más práctica, a partir de la experiencia del Role Carousel.

hours.rationale: PM-2.9 es el único PM protagónico de S5 (Sesión 5 total = 6h directas + 1.5h autónomas). Se asignan 2.0h directas a PM-2.9 incluyendo Role Carousel + E5 evidence + reflexión. Las 4.0h restantes de la sesión cubren Gr 15 connector awareness, revisión consolidada Gr 1-5, 14, homework instructions, y cierre S5→S6.

evidence.name: Language Functions — Competencia Comunicativa Integrada
evidence.description: El aprendiz ejecuta 5 funciones comunicativas en 5 estaciones del Role Carousel (Pixel & Ink Studio), empleando frases fijas apropiadas, al menos 3 conectores (and/but/or/because) y be + adjetivo con precisión A1.1.
evidence.instrument_name: Escala de estimación No 5 — Language Functions (5 criterios × 1 pt)

environment.configuration: 5 estaciones separadas (Role Carousel) + cronómetro visible + connector wall + function cards display
materials: Function cards (5 sets de 8 cards) — FUNC-1 a FUNC-5 con exponents + stress markers
Role Carousel handout (5 estaciones) — scenario + required chunks + connector hint
Connector wall printables (and/but/or/because) con ejemplos de S2-S4
Studio Cards for Spot the Difference (40 cards — 20 pairs A/B con 5 diferencias c/u)
Cause & Effect Graphic Organizer (A4 print, 4 cells)
Escape Room kit (5 clues + USB dummy + Survivor Certificate template)
Language Bank poster (40 chunks categorizados por FUNC-1 a FUNC-5)
Grabadora de audio opcional (para revisión posterior)
environment.instructors: Instructor de inglés técnico (titular) + Técnico especialista (opcional para SCN-E Cliente)

activity_card.quiz_alignment_pm20: PASS — pm-2-0.cuestionario_preview.secciones para MGV G1 son: Reading + Writing + Listening + Vocabulary + Grammar (5 secciones × 5 items × 1pt = 25 pts). Language Functions NO está en el cuestionario — se evalúa vivo como E5 Desempeño 5 pts via Escala de estimación No 5 (Role Carousel). Alineado con master prompt PM-2.9 frontmatter (contributes_to_cuestionario: false).
activity_card.quiz_correction_2026_04_20: Corrección vs borrador previo: se pasó de Language Functions 5 pts/5 items (supuesto canon DIESEL) a 0/0 (canon MGV donde Vocabulary reemplaza Language Functions en E6). La evaluación de Language Functions queda íntegramente en E5 (5 pts live).
activity_card.live_rubric_preview_note: Los items abajo NO son items del Cuestionario Consolidado E6 (Language Functions no contribuye a E6 en canon MGV). Se conservan como GUÍA DE VERIFICACIÓN en vivo para el Role Carousel: 5 prompts que el observador usa para validar dominio funcional en cada estación (0/1/2 por ítem alimenta la Escala de estimación No 5 de E5).

live_verification_prompts.stem: Complete: 'Good morning. ___ Andrés. I am a junior designer.'
Look at the image of a stylus. Write the sentence: '____ a stylus.'
Match each studio object with 2 correct adjectives. (1 pt = 2/2 correct matches)
Put the instructions in order: (a) Save the file. (b) Open the app. (c) Export the logo. (d) Close the app.
A designer says something you do not understand. Write 2 chunks you can use:
live_verification_prompts.correct: Acceptable answers: Repeat please / Again please / Sorry, I do not understand / What is this? (any 2)

fluency_techniques: Post-task delayed feedback with board notes (compile 3-5 typical errors after Carousel, discuss at wrap-up)
Reformulation in wrap-up via 'reformulated summary' of student utterances
accuracy_techniques: Recast sutil en breakdowns communicativos (solo si paran la comunicación)
Clarification request via gesture ('?') antes de corrección explícita

legitimate_l1_uses: Meta-instruction for Role Carousel (15 seconds at the start)
Clarification of 'because' as causal connector (30 seconds)
Emergency check for understanding of rubric E5 criteria (no more than 20 sec)
l1_management.reduction_strategy: From S4 (15%) → S5 (12%): L1 only at transitions, never inside a role station

stress_pronunciation.board_marking_convention: Stressed syllable in CAPITAL LETTERS + UNDERLINE (e.g., beCAUSE)

success_factors_applied.Salience: Language Bank poster + color-coded by function family
success_factors_applied.Use: Minimum 2 uses per chunk per Role Carousel rotation
success_factors_applied.Connection: Each chunk anchored to a character of Pixel & Ink Studio
success_factors_applied.Context: All chunks lived inside 5 studio scenarios
success_factors_applied.Emotion: Gamified via Escape Room + Introduction Chain Round 3
success_factors_applied.Spaced_repetition: Chunks from S1 (greetings) → S2 (colors) → S3 (describing) → S4 (imperatives) → now consolidated
success_factors_applied.Synergy: Chunks combine across functions (Greeting + Repair + Thank you = natural exchange)

wrap_up_s5_autonomous_learning_check.pm29_master_prompt_component: Wrap-up / Review & Autonomous Learning Check (from PM-2.9 master prompt)
wrap_up_s5_autonomous_learning_check.placement: Final 20 minutes of S5 — after E5 evidence collection

structure.activity: Function Family Recap — Language Bank wall review
structure.task: Classes walks by the Language Bank poster. Each student points to ONE chunk they used today and says: 'I used [chunk]. It was easy / difficult.'
Exit ticket: for each of 5 functions, student rates (0/1/2): 'Can I do it alone?' — 0=No / 1=With help / 2=Alone.

Teacher: 'Tomorrow is the GREAT CONSOLIDATION. The test has 5 sections: Reading + Writing + Listening + Language Functions + Grammar. 25 points total. Plus E5 Language Functions (you already got it today) = 5 points. Bring your portfolio.'

Record 90-second video at home: 'Hello. I am [name]. I am a junior designer at Pixel & Ink Studio. My favorite tool is ____ because ____. My favorite color is ____ and ____. Thank you.' Submit via Google Classroom before S6.

wrap_up_s5_autonomous_learning_check.purpose: Cerrar el ciclo de apropiación (S2-S5) y preparar psicológicamente al aprendiz para el Cuestionario Consolidado S6. Transferir la metacognición ('¿qué puedo hacer solo?') como predictor de éxito evaluativo.
